short: US President Woodrow Wilson outlined a vision for a post-war world order based on free trade, democracy, and self-determination.
full:
On 8 January 1918, President Woodrow Wilson delivered a speech to the United States Congress articulating fourteen principles for peace to be used for negotiations to end the First World War. The points called for the abolition of secret treaties, freedom of the seas, free trade, a reduction in armaments, and the readjustment of colonial claims.

The principles also demanded national self-determination for various populations and the creation of a general association of nations. Although Allied leaders were skeptical of Wilson's idealism, the Fourteen Points were heavily publicized and influenced the eventual German decision to seek an armistice, though many of the points were compromised in the final Treaty of Versailles.
